div.div: خَرِيرٌ A depressed tract between two hills, (S, K,) stretching along: (S:) pl. أَخِرَّةٌ. (S, K.) The pl. occurs in a verse of Lebeed, commencing بِأَخِرَّةِ الثَّلَبُوتِ, as Khalaf El-Ahmar heard the Arabs recite it: so says A'Obeyd: (S:) but the common reading is بِأَحِزَّة, with ح and ز. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
